svg.title: Moving time lost to heat, and the cold side we do not model
svg.desc: Moving time lost over a flat 10 km against air temperature, for four effort presets, measured against a neutral baseline of 15 degrees. Below 15 degrees every preset is exactly zero, because no cold penalty is modelled at all, where the published curve is a shallow U with losses on both sides. Above 15 degrees the four presets rise together: at 25 degrees they span 2.19 to 2.52 per cent, and at 32 degrees 3.46 to 4.48 per cent. At 35 degrees easy and steady reach 4.35 and 4.28 per cent, but tempo and race jump to 7.36 and 8.85 per cent, drawn as hollow markers on dashed lines because they are the solver reaching the limit of what is sustainable rather than a smooth physiological curve. The published slope and the Ely quartile figures are given in the footer in wet-bulb globe temperature, not plotted, because they carry no air temperatures.
